question: What if I put 10% in Tesla?

answer.answer: Robert, I tested 10% in Tesla and the portfolio fails your limits (checks C1, G4 and G9). Your real Tesla exposure would be about 10.0%, and the worst drop would be -14.3%, about $57,158. That is just under your 15% loss limit of $60,000. The problem is Tesla itself: its worst drop in 2021-2026 was -70.9%, so at 10% it alone could cost -7.1% of the portfolio, more than one asset may use from your loss limit. Tesla's cap for you is about 3.1%, which gives a worst drop of -9.6% (about $38,241), but even that version still fails two checks (C1 and G4), so it doesn't fully fit your limits either.

why.TSLA: TSLA's worst drop in 2021-2026 was -70.9%; at 10% that alone would be -7.1% of the portfolio, more than the 25% of your 15% loss limit one asset may use; you can hold about 15% in stocks, and one company is kept to 1/5 of that; it fits up to 3.1%
